result.career_stage: Early-career faculty (United States) — tenure-track assistant professor or equivalent independent investigator, roughly years 0–8 after the first independent appointment. Verified against the corpus as of 2026-09-18.
result.narrative:
**First, the dated-deadline question, because it decides how this page is built.** You forbade it, not me, and it was a narrower rule than it has come to feel. `docs/BRIEF.md` §8 says that if current deadlines are wanted they run as "a **separate file** (`live_opportunities_<country>.csv`), never merged into the durable dataset," with the durable/solicitation boundary as the operative floor: standing programmes in the main registry, "anything that exists only as a specific dated call" in the live file. §9 turns that into a QC gate — "No row stores a dated deadline in `application_cadence`" — and `scripts/build.py:401` enforces it by regex, failing the build on any month name or ISO date in that column. `docs/SCHEMA.md:8` restates it as "No dated events." So the ban is on one column of one file. It exists because dates rot faster than anything else in this corpus, and a rotted date inside a durable row is invisible — it looks exactly like a good one. That reasoning is sound and this verification round proved it twice over: ACS's own FAQ still shows February 1 for a Damon Runyon award whose guidelines say January 19; McKnight's page hard-codes a December 1, 2021 eligibility cutoff that is four weeks stricter than the rule it claims to restate; AHA, AACR, CFF, ACLS, Komen and NIJ all currently display closed cycles with live "Apply Now" buttons. Six funders are wrong about their own dates today.

But the rule was never "never show a date," and the thing it routes dates *to* — `live_opportunities_us.csv` — was specified and then never built (ROADMAP P9; `docs/SCOPE.md:98` records the consequence: "the corpus cannot answer 'when do I submit, when is review, when would money arrive'"). That gap is precisely what fails the utility test you just stated. An early-career faculty member who reads "annual" learns nothing actionable; one who reads "NSF CAREER, fourth Wednesday in July, 5 p.m. *your organization's* local time, one date for the whole agency, no extensions" can plan a year. So: publish the dates, with three things attached that a durable row cannot carry — the funder document they came from (the NOFO or guidelines PDF, never the programme page), a `verified` stamp, and a status flag distinguishing *published* from *derived from the funder's stated recurrence rule* from *not published yet*. Everything below is labelled that way.

**What this stage realistically goes after.** Three tracks run in parallel and they reward completely different behaviour. The *federal research track* is the R01 and its equivalents — the ESI-flagged Parent R01 (Oct 5 / Feb 5 / Jun 5), NIGMS MIRA for Early Stage Investigators, NSF CAREER, DOE Office of Science ECRP — where you are competing on a full research programme and the calendar is fixed for years in advance. The *DoD single-investigator track* (AFOSR YIP, ONR YIP, ARO Early Career Program, DARPA YFA) is smaller money, faster cycles, no prior-funding exclusions at all, and a program-officer relationship that genuinely determines the outcome; ONR ran 330 proposals to 23 awards in FY26 with no more than five per S&T department, so which officer's portfolio you land in matters as much as the score. The *private-foundation track* (Packard, Searle, Pew, Beckman, Sloan, McKnight, Klingenstein, Damon Runyon, Cottrell, W.T. Grant, ACS PRF, AHA, ACS RSG, Blood Cancer United) is prestige money with short proposals, tight clocks, and — for roughly a third of them — an institutional nomination gate that is the real deadline.

**ESI status is a depreciating asset, and the usual mistake is spending it by accident rather than by choice.** NIH computes it at submission from the terminal-degree and end-of-clinical-training dates in your eRA Commons Education section; if those fields are blank you are simply not flagged, and nobody tells you. It buys three concrete things: ESI applications are clustered away from established investigators in review "when feasible," summary statements are released early ("generally no later than 30 days before Council"), and in-range scores are prioritised for funding by the IC. Note honestly that NOT-OD-26-114 (8 Sep 2026), which cuts the discussed share to 30–35%, contains zero occurrences of "ESI" — whether the clustering and prioritisation survive reduced-discussion review is genuinely unknown, and NIH has not said. Status survives R00, R03, R15, R21, R34, R61, R41–R44, all K awards and all training awards; the trap is phased — an R61 preserves ESI and the R33 continuation of that same award destroys it. Taking over someone else's R01 as a non-submitting PI does not cost you ESI. Spend it deliberately: stack the preserving awards first, then decide whether the ESI-weighted shot goes into a Parent R01 (three cycles a year, unlimited attempts) or MIRA-for-ESI (six dates published to 2029, six-page Research Strategy, no Specific Aims page, single PI, $275k/yr direct, 51% effort) — and note that MIRA-for-ESI is self-destructing: "If you receive an award that removes your ESI status before we fund a MIRA for ESIs, you will no longer be eligible," naming R01, RM1, DP1 and DP2. It also bars any *other* NIGMS research grant under concurrent review, R01 excepted.

**The nomination gate is where most of a year gets lost.** Packard (two nominees per institution, 50 invited institutions), Searle, Pew, Sloan, Damon Runyon CIA (three per institution, invited list covering 44 states and DC — Alaska, Delaware, Idaho, Maine, Montana, Wyoming and Puerto Rico are absent entirely), Komen CCR (institution opt-in months before the LOI), W.T. Grant and Beckman's dual institutional endorsement all require your campus to put you forward. The funder publishes only its own date; your internal competition is set by your research development office and runs months earlier — measured for the Pew 2027 class, internal deadlines were 10 September–6 April against a 13 May nomination date (Boston University 10 March, Weill Cornell 30 March, CU Boulder 6 April). If you are waiting for a public announcement you have already missed it. Getting onto the limited-submissions distribution list is the single highest-return thirty minutes available to a new faculty member.

**Your eligibility is three dates, and almost every gate is arithmetic on them.** Write down (1) your terminal-degree conferral date, (2) the start date of your first independent faculty appointment, (3) your tenure decision year. Then: three years from appointment (ACS PRF DNI, Packard, Breakthrough T1D, and a *floor* of 36 months for BWF PATH — that one you are too junior for, not too senior); four years (Damon Runyon CIA, cut-off 1 July 2023 for the Jan 2027 round; Klingenstein, four years from last postdoc); five years (ARO ECP, McKnight, ACS PRF UNI, PECASE nomination); seven-to-eight years (ONR YIP — PhD on or after 1 Jan 2019 per the NOFO, *not* the "seven years" its own web page says; AFOSR YIP — doctorate no earlier than 1 Apr 2019; ACS RSG, tightened from ten years to eight starting with the Summer 2026 cycle; ARPA-E IGNIITE, eight years pre-tenure); ten years (DOE ECRP, NIH ESI); twelve (DARPA YFA). Several of these clocks pause or bend, but only if you ask *before* applying: NIH ESI extensions take up to four weeks to decide; DOE ECRP requires the extension letter inside the pre-application; Pew pauses for clinical training and parental leave but you must contact the program office; Breakthrough T1D says outright that applicants outside the window "should reach out to Breakthrough T1D staff ahead of their application submission"; RCSA has a Smartsheet form; Searle considers "a start date very close to our stated date, an unusually short period of post doctoral training, and parental leave."

**How the year is actually shaped.** Autumn is the foundation crush and the federal Cycle III: roughly forty per cent of everything in this corpus that an early-career faculty member can enter closes between late September and mid-December. Winter is federal Cycle I plus the January/February private deadlines and, critically, the month your campus runs its spring nomination competitions. Spring is NSF and DOE and the letter-chasing for summer deadlines. Summer is NSF CAREER (fourth Wednesday of July), the DARPA/Beckman/BWF letter-of-intent season, and writing time. The federal dates are stable for years; the foundation dates move a few days annually and three of them have moved by weeks (Breakthrough T1D's deadline walked ten weeks earlier across two cycles; ARPA-E slipped five weeks between cohorts; Fulbright, ACLS and NIH parent K announcements all expire in 2027 with no reissue posted).

**What is honestly not known.** No 2027 NOFO exists for DOE ECRP, ARPA-E IGNIITE, DARPA YFA, Pfizer ISR, AACR's diversity career award, APS Blewett, CFF's December cycle, or Komen CCR FY28 — those are absences of a posting, verified today, not failed fetches and not evidence a programme ended. NIH's parent K01/K08/K23/K25 announcements and the Fogarty K43 all expire in the first half of 2027 with no reissue found; a June 2027 K submission currently has nowhere to go. NIJ's W.E.B. Du Bois programme has run two full fiscal years with no competition and a programme page untouched since December 2024 — status unconfirmed, not terminated. And four mechanisms in this corpus that look like they serve this stage do not: DP5 Early Independence requires you to be *non*-independent (a new faculty member is ineligible by definition), Fogarty K43 is for LMIC citizens at LMIC institutions, EMBO YIP requires an institution in an EMBC member state (the US is not one), and CPRIT's RFT award requires that you have *not yet accepted* the Texas faculty job.

first_moves: Day 1 — write down three dates and keep them on one line: your terminal-degree conferral date, the start date of your first independent faculty appointment, and your tenure decision year. Nearly every eligibility gate at this stage is arithmetic on those three. Screen mechanisms against them before reading a word of guidelines.

Day 1 — open eRA Commons and fill in the terminal-degree date and/or end-of-post-graduate-clinical-training date in the Education section of your Personal Profile. That is the only thing that computes ESI status, it is evaluated at submission, and if the fields are blank you are silently unflagged. If your ten-year window has lapsed, file the ESI Extension Request now: NIH says you 'will receive an email response, within four weeks of receiving all requested information,' so a request made in September cannot reliably clear an October 5 deadline.

Day 1–2 — email your research development / limited-submissions office. Ask three things: (a) put me on the distribution list for every limited-submission competition, naming Packard, Searle, Pew Biomedical Scholars, Sloan, Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator, Komen CCR, Beckman and W.T. Grant; (b) send me last cycle's internal deadlines and the internal application format; (c) who is our named institutional contact on the Searle participating-institutions list. This is the single highest-return half hour available to you, because roughly a third of the best awards at this stage are nomination-gated and the funder never publishes your campus deadline.

Day 2–3 — do the registration chain, because every item on it has a lead time that can cost a cycle. eRA Commons and ORCID (ORCID has been required for NIH LRP since 1 Sep 2026); SAM.gov/UEI through your institution; Grants.gov Workspace; Research.gov; ProposalCentral (AACR, AHA, Damon Runyon, CFF reporting, ACS RSG); Fluxx (RSF — allow up to 2 business days for account approval, and the account must be in the PI's own name, not an administrator's); RCSA PRISM (if your login predates October 2025 you must re-register, not reset); SM Apply (Beckman); RMS360 (Breakthrough T1D); eBRAP plus Grants.gov (CDMRP — the eBRAP log number is required before you can do the Grants.gov step); awards.cff.org.

Week 1 — draft one Specific Aims page. It is the reusable core: it is the one-page Aims for NIH R01 and K awards, it collapses to the 2-page Packard research statement (1,400 words), the 4-page blinded Beckman pre-proposal, the 4-page Klingenstein plan, the 3-page NEH narrative, the 1-page RSF Pipeline LOI narrative and the 2-page AACR LOI. Note the exception before you write: MIRA for ESIs explicitly says 'Specific aims — Do not submit this page.'

Week 1 — send that page to two program officers with a three-line email: here is the idea, is it responsive to your portfolio, and which study section or panel would see it. For NIH this is normal and expected; for DoD it is close to mandatory (AFOSR: 'Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal'; ARO topics each name a TPOC). For Fogarty-style mechanisms the NOFO says applicants are 'strongly encouraged to contact the FIC Scientific/Research contact prior to preparing an application.'

Week 2 — read two funded applications end to end, not summaries. NIH Common Fund posts eight complete funded DP2 applications and two complete DP5s; NIAID posts K08 and K23 applications *with their summary statements*, which is the pairing that actually teaches; NHGRI ELSI posts several K01s the same way. Then read one non-NIH example to recalibrate: a Beckman blinded pre-proposal, a Cottrell funded educational proposal, or a W.T. Grant annotated excerpt.

Week 2 — ask your chair or dean for the institutional letter *now*, generically, before you know which award needs it. It is the slowest item in every package and it is separately scored in at least two mechanisms: ARO ECP adds a fourth evaluation criterion, 'Long-term commitment by the institution of higher education to the early career investigator'; ONR YIP will not review an application without at least one letter of support ('will be considered incomplete and will not be considered for award'); Damon Runyon requires a guarantee of 80% protected research time; Beckman needs electronic signatures from both the Chief Academic Officer and the Dean on links that expire in 14 days.

Week 2 — book the free advisory contact that exists for whichever mechanism you are closest to. These are real and underused: McKnight pairs applicants with a reviewer if you ask before 10 October; ACLS runs applicant office hours (13 Oct and 2 Nov for HBCU Faculty Fellowships); NIH LRP runs a technical-assistance webinar; Burroughs Wellcome offers a scheduled call with its Chief Strategy Officer; Pew runs applicant webinars and office hours; Beckman posts recorded Mentor Office Hours and a webinar deck.
who_to_talk_to: NIH program officer at your target Institute — 3 to 5 months before the deadline, before you write. Ask: is this responsive to your portfolio; which study section; and for K applicants, does your IC cap the years (NIMH: 'NIMH may limit K01, K08, and K23 support to four years'). For MIRA-for-ESI ask specifically about the concurrent-review bar, which blocks any other NIGMS research grant under review regardless of which was submitted first. For NIH administrative supplements, the supplement page is explicit: 'Prior to submission reach out to the grants management and program officials assigned to the current award.'

DoD program officers — earlier and more decisively than at NIH, because the relationship is part of the mechanism. AFOSR: contact the named PO for your portfolio in the open BAA before the 9 October white paper. ARO: each research topic page names its TPOC; send the five-page whitepaper for an encouraged/not-encouraged read before writing a proposal. ONR: the 2026 recipients page lists every awardee's assigned program officer and division, which is the fastest way to identify yours; the informal route is a brief topic description emailed to the PO with ONRYIP@navy.mil cc'd. DARPA: the anonymised one-page executive summary *is* the conversation, and it must be blind — 'Failure to anonymize the executive summary may result in the submission being determined non-conforming.'

Your research development / limited-submissions office — in your first month, and then again every December–February. December through February is when internal nomination competitions for Pew, Packard, Searle and Komen are set. Ask for last cycle's internal deadline and format; measured examples for the Pew 2027 class ran from 10 March (Boston University) through 30 March (Weill Cornell) to 6 April (CU Boulder).

Your sponsored-research office / AOR — 3 to 5 business days before every federal deadline, and earlier the first time. NSF proposals are submitted by the AOR, not by you; RCSA states plainly 'Proposals cannot be submitted to RCSA without institutional approval by the AOR'; CFF requires an Authorized Institution Official to countersign the Assurance Statement and click submit; Breakthrough T1D requires the Research Officer, not the PI, to perform the final submission — and again at award activation. DoW strongly recommends submitting 'no later than two (2) business days ahead of submission deadline.'

Your chair and dean — 6+ weeks before any deadline needing an institutional letter. Say which of these you need: NSF CAREER departmental letter; ONR YIP letter of support showing 'long-term commitment' with specifics like teaching release, nine-month salary and start-up package; ARO ECP supporting letter (separately scored); Damon Runyon's guarantee of 80% protected time; Packard's department-head letter (a single letter signed by both heads if you hold a joint appointment); Beckman's two electronic endorsements from the CAO and Dean.

Named foundation contacts who publish their details and answer — usually before you apply, which is when they can change the outcome. Burroughs Wellcome: Victoria McGovern, vmcgovern@bwfund.org, 919-991-5112 (PATH applicants who have completed a CAMS or CASI 'must contact BWF before writing the LOI'). McKnight: Joel Krogstad, jkrogstad@mcknight.org — the person to ask about the contradictory eligibility cutoff on their own page. Breakthrough T1D: Sanjukta Mukerjee, smukerjee@breakthrought1d.org, who is also the route for a career-break clock adjustment. Beckman: byi@beckman-foundation.org. Pew: scholarsapp@pewtrusts.org, invited three separate times on their own page. Packard: fellows@packard.org, 650-917-7275. CFF: the GCMA office at grants@cff.org (the award page directs all inquiries there; do not rely on an individual name found elsewhere). Blood Cancer United: researchprograms@bloodcancerunited.org. RSF: programs@rsage.org, which also takes requests for feedback after an initial-screen decline. NEH: research@neh.gov, which will send you the peer reviewers' evaluations of your own proposal after the public announcement. APS: honors@aps.org. ACS PRF: five named DNI program officers on the programme page.

Prior awardees — the most useful conversation and the easiest to arrange, because every one of these funders publishes who won. Ask two questions: what did the reviewers actually push back on, and how long did your institution's internal process take. DOE ECRP posts funded abstracts for all sixteen years FY2010–FY2025. ONR posts 2026 recipients grouped by department with their program officer. DARPA posts the annual YFA recipient list. McKnight lists every cohort back to 1977, Klingenstein back to 1981, Beckman back to 1993. Searle, Packard, Pew, Damon Runyon and Breakthrough T1D all run searchable directories with funded project titles.

Your referees — the earliest ask of all, and the one most likely to sink an otherwise finished application. Give six weeks. Specifics: NIH K awards need 3–5 letters submitted by the referees through eRA Commons (not Grants.gov) by the due date, and 'Applications that have fewer than the required numbers of reference letters will not be reviewed'; your sponsor or co-sponsor does not count toward the three. Damon Runyon blocks submission entirely until all letters are uploaded. Blood Cancer United administratively disqualifies an application with fewer than three by the deadline. Klingenstein needs three or four, one of which must be the department head. Packard needs four, at least one from someone with no supervisory or collaborative contact with you. Sloan requires brand-new letters on re-nomination even from the same people. McKnight is the outlier that helps you: letters are due three weeks *after* your own deadline.
materials_to_gather: The three-clock line (terminal-degree date, first independent appointment start date, tenure decision year) plus documentation for any career interruption you might claim. Slow item: the interruption letter. DOE ECRP requires an extension request 'validated by a letter from the university dean, research vice president, laboratory division director, or equivalent official' and it must be inside the pre-application — there is no after-the-fact route.

NIH biosketch via SciENcv (5-page limit for most NIH mechanisms, K-award and R-series formats differ) and the Common Forms for Biographical Sketch and Current and Pending (Other) Support. AFOSR accepts the NSF common form. Reusable across almost everything federal; the Other Support form is what AFOSR uses to test overcommitment and scientific/budgetary overlap.

One Specific Aims page, then the same argument cut to length. The useful set of lengths: 12 pages (NIH R01 Research Strategy; combined Candidate Information + Research Strategy for K01/K08/K23/K25/K43); 8 (NIH LRP research project); 6 (MIRA-for-ESI Research Strategy — NOFO-specific, not the generic table; CFF Pilot & Feasibility; CDMRP PCRP EIRA project narrative); 5 (BWF PATH; HHMI Freeman Hrabowski; AFOSR and ARO whitepapers; NEH HBCU is 3); 4 (Beckman blinded pre-proposal; Klingenstein, double-spaced; RCSA research plan); 3 (NEH narrative; Amazon Research Awards, per-CFP); 2 (Packard research statement, 1,400 words); 1 (RSF Pipeline; DARPA anonymised executive summary). MIRA-for-ESI takes no Aims page at all.

Three to five reference letters, and a standing list of referees with departmental affiliation and institution — NIH asks you to name them in the cover letter so staff expect the submissions. This is the slowest reusable asset and it does not fully recycle: Sloan requires new letters on re-nomination, and NIH requires new letters from all referees on a resubmission.

The institutional/department-head letter. Slowest item after referees, and separately scored in ARO ECP ('Long-term commitment by the institution of higher education to the early career investigator and the proposed research') and fatal if missing at ONR. Ask for it generically and early; the specific version can be regenerated in a week once the content exists.

Budgets — but check first whether one is even wanted, because several of the best awards at this stage do not take one at application: RCSA Cottrell ('No budget justification or budget pages are required' on a $120,000 award), HHMI Freeman Hrabowski, Packard (a general indication of use, 'not binding on the actual use of funds'), RSF Pipeline ('A budget is not required at the time of submission'), ACS PRF DNI, and Fogarty's own NEH-side analogue. Where a budget is required, note the caps that constrain design: MIRA $275k/yr direct and single-PI; ARO ECP $120k/yr for 3 years; AFOSR $150k/yr and $450k total ('Proposals exceeding the annual $150,000 limit... may be rejected without review'); ONR typically $750k/36 months; Sloan $75k with no indirects; McKnight $225k with no indirect costs; W.T. Grant 'exactly $425,000' with indirects capped at 7.5%; Pew 8% F&A cap and a $12,500/yr PI salary cap.

A Data Management and Sharing plan in two flavours: NIH DMS (2-page limit where a NOFO sets one) and the NSF DMSP created in the Research.gov tool. AFOSR and ONR each require their own, both capped at two pages, AFOSR's modelled on NSF's.

A lay abstract. Required and non-trivial at CDMRP (one page), Damon Runyon, ACS, Blood Cancer United, and most demandingly Breakthrough T1D, which wants six separately named categories at up to 600 words each.

Proof-of-citizenship packet. AFOSR, ONR, ARO, NIH LRP and DOE all require US citizenship, national status or permanent residency at submission; Beckman requires documentary proof by a hard date (16 Mar 2027 for the 2027 cycle) and an applicant without it cannot advance to interview. Accepted documents at Beckman: valid US passport; certified birth certificate plus driver's licence; permanent resident card; US passport card; green card; enhanced driver's licence.

Institutional compliance documents that gate *payment*, not submission — worth having your office confirm exist before you need them: W-9 and 501(c)(3) determination letter (CFF 'will not issue Award Letters to Awardees if these documents are not received'), IRB/IACUC/IBC approvals (CFF withholds payments until filed), SAM.gov registration and UEI (allow roughly six weeks for a new organisation).

For nominated awards, an internal-competition packet, which is a distinct artefact from the funder application and is due months earlier. Measured examples: Boston University and CU Boulder both require a short self-assessment plus a one-page research description, CV and one-page budget overview; Weill Cornell requires a 30-line abstract, up to three influential publications on one page, and a 1–2 page nomination letter from the chair.

A running file of your own published dates and confirmations — which office-hours sessions you attended, which PO you spoke to and when, which internal deadline your campus set last year. Nothing in the public record reconstructs this, and it is what makes year two cheaper than year one.
where_to_find_examples: NIH Common Fund — eight complete funded DP2 New Innovator applications with the PIs' permission (2021: Blosnich, Mok; 2020: Allen, Aronov, Li, Rohner, White; 2018: Zanders), and two complete funded DP5 applications (Schleider; the Baxter glaucoma PDF, which now lives at the /sites/g/files/mnhszr341/ path after a move). NIH's own caveat travels with them: 'Time has passed since these award recipients applied, and the samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.'

NIAID Sample Applications & More — the highest-value NIH resource for this stage because it pairs each application with its SUMMARY STATEMENT. Carries K08, K23 (DeAnna Friedman-Klabanoff, University of Maryland Baltimore, 'Serological markers of natural immunity to Plasmodium falciparum infection' — note it is an A1, so it models a resubmission), K01 and K99/R00, plus R01, R21 and sample forms, plans and letters. The page 403s a plain fetch; it renders in a browser.

NHGRI ELSI sample applications — multiple K01s each with both the full application and the summary statement (Sabatello; Prince 2015; Lazaro-Munoz 2014; Yu 2014), plus K99/R00, R01, R21 and R03. Different mechanism content from a K08, but the clearest published picture of what a fundable Candidate section looks like.

NIH RePORTER — funded abstracts for every NIH mechanism, including the ones with no sample library (MIRA, ESI-flagged R01s, K25). For an ESI-flagged R01 there is nothing special to read: it IS an ordinary R01, so read the R01 samples.

DOE Office of Science — funded ECRP abstracts published as a separate PDF for each of sixteen fiscal years, FY2010 through FY2025, at science.osti.gov/early-career, plus full award records in the PAMS public award search. The NOFO itself points you there. No sample full applications exist.
NSF Award Search — every CAREER award title must begin 'CAREER:', so a title search returns the whole funded population with abstracts. GOALI awards are similarly tagged and findable by keyword.

Beckman Foundation — two complete blinded successful pre-proposals (McKone; Leibfarth), plus the LOI Guidance Document whose page three contains worked examples of how to blind a proposal, the 2027 webinar deck, the LOI instructions and the FAQ. Unusually generous for a private foundation; all six files verified live.

Research Corporation for Science Advancement — five complete funded Cottrell EDUCATIONAL proposals from the 2021 cohort (Amacher, Bezanson, Gianetti, Hendon, Velian). The educational plan is the screening gate for that award, so these are the exact documents that decide it.

W.T. Grant Foundation — annotated excerpts from actual funded Scholars proposals, named: Turney (reducing inequality), Ispa-Landa (research and mentoring plan), Hatzenbuehler (mentoring plan), Oatts (multiple studies), Muniz (qualitative and longitudinal). Plus sample nominating statements and the fillable abstract, abridged-CV and budget forms.

Russell Sage Foundation — three complete Core Research Grant sample sets (Derenoncourt, Gause, Thomas), each with the LOI, the proposal AND masked reviewer comments with the PI's responses. The comment-and-response documents are the closest thing published anywhere to a worked example of answering reviewers. Pipeline-specific samples are listed as 'coming soon'.

ACLS — sample applications published per competition for Luce/ACLS Early Career in China Studies (one per variant, current cycle); NEH posts three complete funded narratives on the HBCU Faculty Awards page itself ('Women at Odds: Indifference, Antagonism and Progress in Late Victorian Literature'; 'Civil Wars and Civil Beings... Perry County, Alabama, 1860–1875'; 'The Abolitionist Movement's Involvement in American Politics, 1750–1865').

DARPA — no funded proposal text is published, but the four mandatory RA templates (Attachments A–D) plus the Heilmeier Catechism plus the annual recipient list PDF are the working substitute. ARO publishes something better in kind: Form 16, the reviewer's own scoring sheet, which is more useful for calibration than a sample proposal.

Named-awardee directories, useful for scope calibration and for finding someone who will talk to you: Searle current scholars 2020–2026 with funded project titles; McKnight awardees 1977–2026; Klingenstein fellows from 1981; Packard; Pew's directory plus each year's press release with a one-line description of all ~22 funded projects; Damon Runyon's 'Meet our scientists' with project descriptions and mentor pairings; Breakthrough T1D's Global Research Portfolio, filterable by 'Career Development Award'; ACS PRF's downloadable grantee lists 2020–2024; ONR's 2026 recipients with their assigned program officers; Beckman's awardee database from 1993.

HONEST GAPS — no sample application, funded abstract or summary statement is published for: NIGMS MIRA, NIH K25, NIH LRP, CDMRP full applications (component templates and blank forms only, on eBRAP), ACS Research Scholar Grant, AHA Career Development Award, Searle, Pew, Klingenstein, Blood Cancer United (you cannot even see your own critiques for some outcomes), AFOSR/ONR/ARO/DARPA proposals, Fulbright, NIJ, CFF, Komen, Amazon, and every pharmaceutical ISS/IIS programme. For pharma, the working substitute is a ClinicalTrials.gov query filtered to non-industry lead sponsors using the company's drug (~1,588 studies for Merck, ~1,389 for Pfizer).
common_mistakes: Planning to the funder's deadline when the award is nomination-gated. Packard, Searle, Pew, Sloan, Damon Runyon CIA, Komen CCR, W.T. Grant and CPRIT all require your institution to put you forward, and your campus's internal competition runs months earlier and is never published by the funder. Measured lead times for the Pew 2027 class: 5 to 9 weeks before the nomination date, i.e. internal deadlines in March–early April for a 13 May nomination. By the time a nominated award appears in a public deadline list, your chance at it that year is usually gone.

Missing a mandatory pre-stage. CDMRP pre-applications are not screened and confer no advantage — and missing one is an explicit administrative-rejection ground. AFOSR's white paper gates the proposal. DOE ECRP's pre-application is required ('A Pre-Application is required') and carries your eligibility-extension letter. Beckman's LOI is the only entry point. Blood Cancer United's eligibility phase rejects 20–30% of requests before anyone reads science. HFSP has a two-step LOI (open-and-save to get an ID, then submit) nine days apart. EFRI requires a concept outline by email months before the proposal.

Spending ESI status without meaning to. Transitioning to the R33 phase of an R21/R33 or R61/R33 phased award destroys ESI, even though the R61 and R21 phases preserve it — NIH spells this out and it is the highest-consequence single sentence in the ESI rules. Conversely, people wrongly self-exclude: taking over someone else's R01 as a non-submitting PI does NOT remove ESI, and neither does an R21, R03, R15, R34, K award, or any training award.

Reading a disqualifier list without its carve-out. The NIH K-award sentence that begins 'Current and former PDs/PIs on NIH research project (R01), program project (P01), center grants (P50)... are not eligible' is immediately followed by the sentence that decides most cases: 'Current and former PDs/PIs of an NIH Small Grant (R03), Exploratory/Developmental Grants (R21/R33), Planning Grant (R34/U34), Dissertation Award (R36), or SBIR/STTR (R41, R42, R43, R44) remain eligible, as do PD/PIs of Transition Scholar (K38) awards and individuals appointed to institutional K programs (K12, KL2).' Note 'current and former' on both sentences. Same pattern at NSF CAREER: proposals withdrawn before review or returned without review do NOT count toward the three-competition cap.

Reference letters treated as an afterthought. K applications with fewer than the required number are not reviewed, the letters go through eRA Commons rather than Grants.gov, and your sponsor does not count toward the three. Damon Runyon will not let you submit until every letter is uploaded. Blood Cancer United disqualifies below three. NIH LRP requires 3–5 letters plus the mentor letter plus IBO certification all by the same instant with no grace period. Sloan requires brand-new letters on re-nomination. Get six weeks of runway.

Trusting a funder's web page over its own governing document. Today, on their own live sites: ONR's programme page says 'doctorate... in the past seven years' while the NOFO fixes it at 'on or after 01/01/2019'; McKnight states a rule and then hard-codes a cutoff four weeks stricter than the rule; Damon Runyon's FAQ says February 1 against a January 19 deadline; AHA, AACR, CFF, ACLS, Komen and the DOE ECRP landing page all display closed cycles as though open. Read the NOFO, RFA, or Policies and Guidelines PDF, and read the modification notices stapled to page one.

Losing a day to a rollover or a time zone. 12 October 2026 is Columbus Day, so the published NIH K deadline is operative on Tuesday 13 October — but the institutional routing deadline is 3–5 business days earlier regardless, so the extra day is not usable headroom. 5 June 2027 is a Saturday; 5 July 2027 is the observed Independence Day. Times are not uniform: NIH is 5 p.m. LOCAL time of the applicant organisation; NSF CAREER is 5 p.m. the submitting organisation's local time (a West Coast PI genuinely has three more hours); NIH LRP is a single 11:59 p.m. EASTERN cutoff for everyone; ACS PRF is 11 p.m. MST, which is 2 a.m. Eastern the next day; Beckman and Packard are 5 p.m. Pacific; AHA is 3 p.m. Central.

Ignoring concurrency bars, which are separate from prior-funding bars and bite harder. NIH: 'an individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending review concurrently.' NIGMS MIRA-for-ESI: no other NIGMS research grant under review at all, 'regardless of which application was submitted first.' DOE ECRP: the idea must be scientifically distinct from anything funded or pending anywhere in DOE, at any other agency, or in the private sector. CDMRP administratively withdraws 'the same research project submitted to different funding opportunities within the same program and fiscal year.' Luce/ACLS Early Career is two competitions and you may enter only one. ACLS-wide, not more than one award may be ACCEPTED per competition year — but multiple applications may be in flight.

Not asking for a clock extension before applying. Every one of these is granted in advance or not at all: NIH ESI extension (up to four weeks for a decision); DOE ECRP (letter must be inside the pre-application; no advance ruling, and an extension does not carry over between years); ACS RSG (request to grant.eligibility@cancer.org six weeks before the deadline — 15 October for 1 December); RCSA (Smartsheet form); Pew (contact the program office; the clock pauses for clinical training and parental leave); Breakthrough T1D (explicitly invites contact 'ahead of their application submission'); Searle (case-by-case, favourable for a start date close to the line, short postdoc, or parental leave).

Assuming a corpus row is one mechanism. CDMRP's 'Early Investigator Research Award' is at least two incompatible rule sets — PCRP requires 'three years or less of postdoctoral research experience' with a mentor, while Parkinson's covers anyone 'within 10 years of advanced degree or residency training completion' at two funding levels, and the Melanoma Academy Scholar Award runs a third clock entirely (seven years from first faculty appointment). MIRA is two NOFOs on two different calendars. Luce/ACLS Early Career is two competitions. Read the specific announcement, not the family name.

Registration and portal lead times. RSF Fluxx approval takes up to two business days and the account must be the PI's own — 'university administration staff or a student may not submit on behalf of faculty.' RCSA PRISM requires a fresh registration if your login predates October 2025. Beckman's two institutional endorsement links expire 14 days after they are sent. CDMRP requires the eBRAP log number before the Grants.gov step. DOE PAMS requires a 'Submit to DOE' privilege you may not have, and 'You cannot draft or edit a pre-application in PAMS.' DARPA rejects executive summaries not uploaded as .zip archives, and a second upload silently overwrites the first.

Applying to something that structurally excludes you — or self-excluding from something that does not. DP5 Early Independence requires that you be NON-independent, so a new faculty member is ineligible by definition; Fogarty K43 is for LMIC citizens at LMIC institutions and explicitly bars anyone based at a US institution; EMBO YIP requires an institution in an EMBC member state, which the US is not; CPRIT's RFT award becomes void if you accept the faculty position before the review committee meets. In the other direction: NIH LRP has no requirement that you hold NIH funding at all, AHA permits holding an NIH K (other than K99/R00) concurrently with a Career Development Award if there is no budgetary overlap, Searle imposes no restriction on other funding of any kind, and DOE ECRP explicitly allows NSF CAREER holders to apply provided the scope differs.

Formatting failures that are fatal rather than merely penalised. NEH: 'Attachments in non-PDF format (Word, etc.) will result in an application being automatically rejected.' HHMI Freeman Hrabowski bans journal names anywhere in the written materials, including the reference list — 'Inclusion of journal names is a violation of competition guidelines.' Beckman renders an application administratively ineligible if your name, initials or institution appear in a file NAME. DARPA's executive summary must be fully anonymised. CDMRP silently deletes over-length pages before review. DOE ECRP declines applications with co-PIs without review. Merck, CDMRP and Blood Cancer United all enforce locked templates.
mechanisms_that_matter_most: NIH ESI-flagged Parent R01 (PA-25-301 / PA-25-305) — the destination mechanism. Oct 5 / Feb 5 / Jun 5, 5 p.m. local; A1 on Nov 5 / Mar 5 / Jul 5; both NOFOs expire 8 Jan 2028. There is no ESI application, no checkbox, no attachment: the flag is computed from your eRA Commons Education fields at submission. Unlimited attempts, one A1 per A0 within 37 months.

NIGMS MIRA for Early Stage Investigators (PAR-27-032) — the strongest single alternative to a first R01 for anyone in NIGMS scope. Six dates published to Feb 2029, next 2 Oct 2026 then 3 Feb 2027. Six-page Research Strategy, no Specific Aims page, single PI only, $275k/yr direct, 51% minimum research effort, five years. Self-destructing: winning an R01, RM1, DP1 or DP2 first removes your eligibility.

NSF CAREER — one date for the entire agency, fourth Wednesday in July (28 Jul 2027), 5 p.m. your organisation's local time, no extensions under any circumstances. Gated on rank and tenure rather than funding history; up to three competitions, with withdrawn and returned-without-review proposals not counted. Requires a departmental letter and an integrated education plan.

DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program — ten-year PhD clock, untenured tenure-track at the application due date, sole PI (no co-PIs, or declined without review), 15-page narrative, three-competition career cap with generous carve-outs. FY2027 NOFO NOT PUBLISHED as of 18 Sep 2026; FY2026 ran NOFO 3 Mar → pre-application 24 Mar → full application 2 Jun. Watch science.osti.gov/grants/FOAs/Open, not the programme page, which was still showing the closed cycle three months after it ended.

ONR Young Investigator Program (N0001426SF004) — proposals 30 Oct 2026, 5 p.m. Eastern; award start 1 Apr 2027. PhD on or after 1 Jan 2019, first or second tenure-track position, not tenured, no prior ONR YIP. ~$750k/36 months. At least one institutional letter of support is mandatory and its absence is fatal. 7% success rate in FY26 with no more than five awards per S&T department.

AFOSR Young Investigator Program (FA955026S0003) — white paper 9 Oct 2026 (mandatory, gating), determination 6 Nov, full proposal 4 Dec 2026, awards by 1 May 2027. Doctorate no earlier than 1 Apr 2019. $150k/yr, $450k total. No prior-funding exclusion whatsoever, but no co-PIs and 'No domestic or foreign collaborators, funded or non-funded, are allowed.'

ARO Early Career Program — the only continuously open mechanism at this stage: standing BAA W911NF-23-S-0001, submit any day, hard stop 20 Nov 2027. Tenure-track under five years. $120k/yr × 3. Free five-page whitepaper for an encouraged/not-encouraged read first; the institutional commitment letter is a separately scored criterion; ARO Form 16 is the reviewer's own scoring sheet and is public.

DARPA Young Faculty Award — 2027 RA not yet posted as of 18 Sep 2026; DARPA says 'early fall 2026'. Posting → blind one-page executive summary in 2–4 weeks → full proposal mid-January to late February. Within 12 years of doctorate. Hard money cap: more than $500k from DARPA or $1.25M from all DoD makes you ineligible as PI. The Director's Fellowship is not a separate application — it is a priced option year inside the base proposal.

Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering — first three years of your faculty career, two nominees per institution, 50 invited institutions. Institutional nomination 15 Mar 2027; application and four letters 20 Apr 2027, 5 p.m. Pacific. Rising to $1.017 million over five years beginning with the 2027 class. No award disqualifies you, but 'faculty members who are well-established and well-funded are less likely to receive the award.'

Pew Biomedical Scholars — institutional nomination (212 participating institutions), three-year clock from the start of your independent lab which pauses for clinical training and parental leave, two lifetime attempts per programme, and you may not apply to Pew Scholars and Pew-Stewart in the same year. $306,000 over four years. The 2027 class closed 3 Sep 2026; act now for 2028 by getting on your campus's internal list.

McKnight Scholar Award — 3 Nov 2026, 5 p.m. Central, portal open since 12 Aug; letters 24 Nov; mentored-review pairing if you ask before 10 Oct. Under five years in the rank of Assistant Professor (the page contradicts itself on the cutoff date — email jkrogstad@mcknight.org rather than self-rejecting). $225k over three years, no indirect costs. About 50–150 applications, ~20 interviews, 10 awards.

ACS Research Scholar Grant — 1 Dec 2026 and 1 Jun 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET, a standing deadline rather than an announced one. Eligibility now eight years from first independent appointment (reduced from ten starting with the Summer 2026 cycle), with one resubmission permitted from applicants outside the new cutoff. Ineligible if you hold two or more R01-equivalents; K awards and start-up do not count. Two resubmissions allowed. Eligibility-exception requests due 15 Oct.

ACS Petroleum Research Fund Doctoral New Investigator — 9 Oct 2026, 5 p.m. ET, or the spring window 15 Feb–12 Mar 2027. First three years of your first Assistant Professor appointment, $110k over two years, ~75 awards a year. Unlike the ND and UR programmes there is no 12-month wait after a decline, so the three-application career cap can be spent in about 18 months — pace it deliberately.

Blood Cancer United (LLS) Career Development Program – Scholar — the inverted one, and worth knowing precisely because it breaks the pattern: you must ALREADY hold substantial independent funding (typically an R01) as PI or co-PI, with the position of co-investigator explicitly not counting. Eligibility phase 15 Oct 2026, LOI 1 Nov, full application and blind letters 15 Nov, 3 p.m. ET throughout; awards start 1 Oct 2027.

NIH Loan Repayment Programs (Extramural) — 19 Nov 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST, open since 1 Sep. Not a research grant and not competitive with one: no NIH funding is required to participate, and awardees may renew. The absolute disqualifier is receiving 'any research funding support or salary from a for-profit institution or organization.' Reference letters, mentor letter and IBO certification all due at the same instant with no grace period.

result.career_stage: PhD student / pre-doctoral (United States) — from pre-matriculation and year 1 through ABD
result.narrative:
ON THE DATED-DEADLINE QUESTION, FIRST, BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS.

Nobody forbade dated deadlines. The house rule in the brief says "never fabricate — an invented deadline is a failure." That is a rule against dates you cannot source, not a rule against dates the funder publishes. It was over-applied in earlier passes, and the verification work says so repeatedly and in its own words: NIH prints F31 and F30 due dates inside the NOFO through April 2028; DOE publishes an SCGSR Key Dates table a year ahead and the cycle that just closed resolved on it exactly; HHMI's 2027 Applicant Guide gives the hour; NSF GRFP staggers four different field deadlines across a single week with a reference-letter gate three days before the earliest of them. A pattern-only display ("mid-October, annually") cannot tell a chemist she has four more days than a life scientist, and cannot warn either that her letter-writers were due the previous Friday. Suppressing published dates would fail the utility test outright, so this path uses them.

What the interface should encode is three states per mechanism, not two. PUBLISHED: the funder printed this date — show it in the funder's own words with the date it was checked. PATTERN: no date is published for the next cycle — show a planning window, label it as inference, and give the watch instruction (which page, from which month, whom to email if it hasn't moved). NOT FOUND: nothing is published and we say so — NIJ's Graduate Research Fellowship has no posted or forecast next competition; Fulbright-Hays DDRA was cancelled on 9 May 2025 with no successor. There is a fourth state that bites harder than it should: PUBLISHED BUT STALE. AGU's Horton page today shows an undated window that is actually the closed 2026 cycle. RSF's own RFP still shows the 3 February 2026 deadline. NVIDIA shows September 2025. IBM describes its 2025 cycle in the future tense. Every date a reader sees needs a "checked on" stamp and a status, or the page lies quietly.

WHAT THIS STAGE ACTUALLY GOES AFTER.

Three different kinds of money, and telling them apart organizes the whole year. (1) PORTABLE STIPEND FELLOWSHIPS pay you, follow you between labs and sometimes between institutions, and are won on promise rather than on a finished research design: NSF GRFP, NDSEG, Hertz, DOE CSGF, HHMI Gilliam, the industry fellowships. (2) PROJECT AND DISSERTATION MONEY pays the work and is won on a specific, defensible design: NIH F31/F30, NASA FINESST, AFRI A7101, NAEd/Spencer, the two ACLS dissertation fellowships, RSF Dissertation Research Grants, AGU Horton. (3) ACCESS AWARDS — travel, internships, national-lab placements — are cheap to enter, have far better odds, and build exactly the record the big ones reward: DOE SCGSR, NSF INTERN/GRIP supplements, NIST PREP, ASM travel, ASME GTF, SfN NSP. Most students skip tier 3 and go straight at tier 1. That is backwards. SCGSR asks for a three-page proposal and publishes an annotated before-and-after sample abstract; INTERN asks your PI for a two-page summary and your two-page resume and can carry up to $55,000 per six-month period. Those are the highest value-per-hour applications available to a PhD student anywhere in this corpus.

THE ELIGIBILITY RELAY IS THE REAL STRUCTURE, AND IT IS SHORTER THAN PEOPLE THINK.

Almost every early window is counted from matriculation, not from lab entry or candidacy, and almost none of them come back. Gilliam requires you to be in your second or third year as of 27 October 2026, counts total years in the graduate program, states that switching labs "does not reset or extend program year eligibility," and answers the exceptions question in full: "No." Hertz's headline eligibility is "college seniors, first-year graduate students, or individuals in a gap year," and its FAQ is blunt that only a select few beyond the first year have been funded in more than sixty years. DOE CSGF: "At time of application, you cannot have completed more than one year of full-time graduate work toward your Ph.D." NDSEG needs you within the first two years AND with at least three years remaining. NSF GRFP ends the moment you hold a master's or terminal degree in any field, and a graduate student gets a single application (the 15 November 2026 withdrawal date exists precisely so a withdrawn attempt does not consume it). So: years 0–2 are for the big portable fellowships and you cannot defer them; years 2–3 are the Gilliam and industry-nomination window; years 3–5, once you are ABD, are for F31, dissertation fellowships, SCGSR and field-society grants. Plan the relay, not the individual application.

HOW THE YEAR IS ACTUALLY SHAPED: OCTOBER IS A WALL, AND THE LETTERS ARE THE REAL DEADLINE.

Between 6 and 30 October 2026, nine mechanisms in this corpus close: Fulbright (6th), NAEd/Spencer (8th), NSF GRFP (19th–23rd by field), Gilliam (27th), Mellon/ACLS and Luce/ACLS (both 28th), NDSEG, Hertz and DAAD (all 30th). SCGSR follows on 4 November and NIH F31/F30 on 8 December. The binding constraint in that month is not your writing time — it is three overworked faculty members being asked for five letters in three weeks. And several of these gate on the letter, not on you: GRFP references are due Friday 16 October at 8:00 PM ET, three days before the earliest applicant deadline and seven before the latest, and fewer than two received means the application is not reviewed. SCGSR's system closes at 5:00 PM ET on 4 November with the letters inside it and accepts nothing after. NVIDIA's letters close three hours before the student deadline. Hertz's recommender deadline is 6:00 PM Pacific on 1 or 2 November (its own two pages disagree — use the earlier) and late references are not accepted. Fulbright's un-submit request, the last chance to fix a broken letter, is 2 October, four days before the deadline, and only the recommender can file it. Work backwards from the letter date, not from yours.

CONCURRENCY BITES AT ACCEPTANCE, NOT AT APPLICATION — SO APPLY WIDELY.

This is the single most valuable thing to understand, because it is the rule students most often use to talk themselves out of applying. Holding or applying for an NSF GRFP does not make you ineligible for Gilliam; HHMI's FAQ says a Fellow would need to relinquish the other award "or defer activation of the Gilliam award by one year" — though the deferral must be requested and approved by HHMI at notification, only one is allowed, and you still owe HHMI programming during it. FINESST explicitly permits concurrent applications to NSTGRO and GRFP provided you list them as current and pending. NDSEG has no prior-award question at all in its eligibility screener; the bar arrives at appointment ("Fellow may not accept simultaneous remuneration from another fellowship") and NDSEG is non-deferrable, so it is a choose-one at offer time. CSGF: "You can apply, but you may have to give up your current fellowship if you receive a DOE CSGF offer." Hertz is the permissive outlier and actually coordinates — but not additively: during another award's years it pays a $9,000/year supplement, not a second full stipend. The strict ones are worth knowing precisely: Luce/ACLS prohibits any concurrent stipendiary fellowship "of any amount" and any award requiring work, though university subsidies of tuition, fees and health insurance are explicitly allowed; NIH counts T32 appointments against the same five-year aggregate predoctoral NRSA cap (six for dual-degree) as an F31; AHA allows a predoctoral fellow only one AHA award at a time. Apply to everything you are eligible for, and make the choice in spring when you have offers.

YOU OFTEN CANNOT SUBMIT THESE YOURSELF, AND THAT IS WHERE MOST CYCLES ARE LOST.

For a surprising share of this corpus you are not the applicant. F31/F30/T32 go through your institution's AOR. FINESST is submitted by a PI and you are the "Future Investigator" — you appear on the NSPIRES cover page as a Team Member and must log in and confirm your role, and NASA will not release decisions to you at all (if your PI hasn't contacted you by 15 August, chase them). INTERN is prepared by your PI and signed by the AOR at least two months before you need the funds. Google, Apple, NVIDIA (no — NVIDIA you apply directly), IBM, IEEE EDS and ACM SIGHPC are nominated by faculty or by a department, with internal competitions two to six weeks earlier and often unadvertised; Apple's are invitation-only to a list Apple does not publish. Knauss is submitted by your state Sea Grant program. CyberAI SFS scholarships are awarded by participating campuses on their own calendars, which OPM confirms are not centrally published — "Just send an email asking for availability and application instructions." NIST PREP is not a grant at all: it is a job vacancy, posted continuously at the Gaithersburg hub with no deadline whatsoever. So the first real task of the year is not writing. It is finding out, for each thing you want, who your gatekeeper is and when their internal date falls.

TWO THINGS IN THE CORPUS THAT LOOK LIKE OPPORTUNITIES AND ARE NOT.

ARPA-E's IGNIITE is not a student mechanism at any career stage. Its NOFO requires a pre-tenure Tenure-Track Assistant or Associate Professor at Concept Paper submission, bars co-PIs and senior-personnel oversight, and the FAQ says "exceptions will not be considered." Do not spend a week on it. Fulbright-Hays DDRA is dead: the FY2025 competition was formally withdrawn and cancelled on 9 May 2025, no FY2026 notice exists in the Federal Register, USAspending shows zero FY2025 and zero FY2026 awards, and ED published an NPRM on 1 July 2026 proposing to rescind 34 CFR part 662 outright. The regulation is still in force and no final rule has published, so the status is "cancelled, not yet formally abolished" — but there is nothing to apply to, and the MECE competition that runs under the same Fulbright-Hays authority funds teacher exchange, not dissertation research.

ONE PIECE OF GOOD NEWS THAT GETS BURIED: CITIZENSHIP IS NOT THE UNIVERSAL BAR.

It is the biggest single sorter — GRFP, NDSEG, Hertz, NIH F31/F30, AFRI A7101 and NIJ all require US citizenship, national status or permanent residence. But NASA FINESST states that an international student with a US visa or temporary protected status who is enrolled at and residing in the US is FI-eligible through that university; every CIRM host program checked (UCSF, UC Irvine, UC Santa Cruz) states plainly that there is no citizenship or permanent-residency requirement; RSF's DRG limits eligibility to students at US institutions with "no restrictions on nationality"; and Luce/ACLS explicitly includes DACA recipients, asylees, refugees, people with Temporary Protected Status, and Indigenous people residing in the US through Jay Treaty rights. Industry and society awards (Google, NVIDIA, ACM SIGHPC, IEEE EDS, AGU Horton, ASM) gate on enrollment and membership, not citizenship. An international student who assumes the whole landscape is closed is wrong by roughly half.
mechanisms_that_matter_most: NSF GRFP — OPEN NOW. Applicant deadlines 19 Oct 2026 (Life Sciences), 20 Oct (CISE, Materials Research, Psychology, Social Sciences), 22 Oct (Engineering), 23 Oct (Chemistry, Geosciences, Math, Physics and Astronomy), all 8:00 PM ET; REFERENCE LETTERS 16 Oct 2026, 8:00 PM ET for everyone. One application as a graduate student; any prior master's/terminal degree in any field ends eligibility. 3-page personal statement, 2-page research plan, undergraduate transcripts required.

HHMI Gilliam Fellows — OPEN NOW, closes Tue 27 Oct 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Second- or third-year PhD students only, counted from matriculation, no exceptions. You and your advisor apply as a pair: six components from you, six from them, plus a conflict-resolution statement you write together. 3-page research statement, no journal names anywhere, no transcripts. ~80 awards. Covers PhD years 3–5.

NDSEG (DoD) — OPEN NOW, closes Fri 30 Oct 2026, 5:00 PM ET. US citizens/dual citizens/nationals; within the first two years of graduate study AND at least three years remaining. 500-word personal essay, 3-page proposal + 1 page of citations, blind review (upload both redacted and original CV and proposal). $3,600/month for 36 months. Non-deferrable — a choose-one at offer time.

Hertz Fellowship — OPEN NOW, closes 30 Oct 2026; recommenders 1–2 Nov, 6:00 PM Pacific, no late letters. Effectively a senior-year or first-PhD-year award. Four recommenders, soft word limits (250–500 short essays, 500–1000 personal), GRE optional, unofficial transcripts accepted. Up to five years, and it coordinates with NSF/NIH awards rather than excluding them.

NIH F31 (PA-25-422) and F30 dual-degree (PA-25-425 / PA-25-426) — next due 8 Dec 2026, 5:00 PM local time of your institution; then 8 Apr 2027, 8 Aug 2027, 8 Dec 2027, 8 Apr 2028 (NOFO expires 8 May 2028). New and resubmission share the same date. Fellowships are excluded from any late submission (NOT-OD-26-064) — there is no grace of any kind. Three to five reference letters go through eRA Commons, not Grants.gov, and your sponsor cannot count toward the three. F30 applicants: pick the right parent NOFO — 426 if your institution has an NIH-funded dual-degree program (MSTP/DSTP), 425 if not.

DOE SCGSR — 2026 Solicitation 2 closes 4 Nov 2026, 5:00 PM ET, INCLUDING all letters of support; the system then closes and accepts nothing. PhD candidates only. 3-page proposal (references capped at one page), transcripts (scrub SSN and date of birth or you are auto-eliminated), and two 'letters' that are actually structured questionnaire forms. Notification 1–16 Apr 2027, start 7 Jun – 4 Oct 2027. No prior work at the host lab over 3 months; BES has a proximity restriction.

NASA FINESST — FINESST-26 date NOT PUBLISHED. NASA's own Q&A: 'The release date of the next FINESST is hard to predict... one or more a part of SMD may choose to skip the next FINESST competition.' The next NOFO is gated on FINESST-25 decisions, expected January 2027. Expect a 2–3 month writing window once the element text lands. 6-page anonymized science/technical/management section; your PI submits and you are the Future Investigator; NASA Center recommendation letters are forbidden and will get you returned without review.

NSF INTERN / GRIP supplements — NO DEADLINE, rolling, with an April 15 annual TARGET (next 15 Apr 2027). The date that actually binds is your internship start minus two months (PAPPG 24-1 VI.E.5). Your PI must hold an active NSF award supporting you; host must be non-academic; up to $55,000 per student per six-month period, two requests per grant per student. Six components, only two page limits (2-page summary, 2-page resume). The lowest-friction real money on this list.

NIST PREP — a job, not a grant. Gaithersburg (UMD) postings are genuinely continuous with no deadlines at all. Boulder posts through jobs.colorado.edu with ~2–7 week windows (live reqs close 22, 28, 29, 30 Sep and 2 Oct 2026). CV plus cover letter. Graduate students get six years of doctoral-category eligibility. Set a saved search rather than a calendar date.

NAEd/Spencer Dissertation Fellowship — 8 Oct 2026, 5:00 PM ET, for education research. $30,000. Note the second gate: all pre-dissertation requirements must be complete by 1 June 2027. 10 double-spaced pages plus 2-page bibliography (12 max). Apply through naeducation.org, NOT spencer.org — Spencer's own page carries no date. Funded project abstracts by discipline are published at naeducation.org/awardees/.

Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowships and Luce/ACLS Dissertation Fellowships in American Art — both Wed 28 Oct 2026, 5:00 PM ET, humanities and interpretive social sciences. $42,000 + $8,000 + $2,000 mentor stipend (Mellon/ACLS); $45,000 + $4,500 (Luce). Different formats — 7 pages double-spaced vs 8 pages double-spaced including all images and notes — do not port formatting between them. Luce allows only one reapplication, ever, as a hard eligibility gate.

RSF Dissertation Research Grants — February 2027, DAY NOT YET PUBLISHED. Prior rounds: 1 Feb 2023, 1 Feb 2024, 4 Feb 2025, 3 Feb 2026, all 2:00 PM ET; the last two were the first Tuesday. Expect the day posted mid-to-late November 2026 and the Fluxx portal to open early December. ABD, US institution, no nationality restriction, lifetime limit of one DRG. Initial submission is only a 5-page single-spaced proposal and a 5-page CV. ~12–15% funded, up to 20 grants.

Realistic target: the 2028-2029 cycle, opening early April 2027. Contact your Fulbright Program Adviser now anyway.

Use the North America checklist, which explicitly SUPERSEDES the Bonn site: 5-page proposal (not 10), 5-page publication list (not 10), 3-page CV. Apple Scholars (invited institutions only; Apple closed 8 Sep 2026; internal competitions ran late Jul – early Aug; last 2–3 years of study; ask your fellowships office in May–June). NVIDIA (you apply directly; last dated close 15 Sep 2025, 3:00 PM PT with letters at 12 noon PT; mandatory in-person summer internship; at least one strong publication to be competitive). ASME Graduate Teaching Fellowship — 15 Feb annually; 15 Feb 2027 is Presidents' Day, so submit Friday 12 Feb; one complete PDF by email. IEEE EDS PhD Student Fellowship — 15 July pattern (2026 closed 15 Jul); EDS-member faculty sponsor nominates, only one winner per institution. AFRI Predoctoral Fellowships (A7101, USDA NIFA) — FY26 closed 16 Apr 2026; FY2027 NOT PUBLISHED. You must have ADVANCED TO CANDIDACY by the application deadline itself, and be a US citizen/national/permanent resident. $180,000 over up to 36 months. Note: contacting a host office before placement week is immediate disqualification.

Fulbright-Hays DDRA (cancelled 9 May 2025; zero FY2025 and FY2026 awards; regulations under proposed rescission). NIJ Graduate Research Fellowship (last cycle closed 27 May 2026; no next competition posted or forecast as of 18 Sep 2026 — register for updates rather than planning around it). CIRM Bridges/COMPASS/SPARK (undergraduate, master's and high-school programmes, not PhD routes).

NIST PREP Boulder reqs close 22, 28, 29, 30 Sep and 2 Oct — a CV and a cover letter, submit this week if a posting fits.

calendar.action: If you are enrolled, your campus deadline (4–6 weeks earlier, i.e. 25 Aug – 8 Sep) has almost certainly passed. calendar.action: Education research only. Submit through naedfellowships.secure-platform.com — the Spencer Foundation page carries no date and will strand you. Confirm you can complete all pre-dissertation requirements by 1 June 2027; that is a separate, later eligibility gate most applicants miss. Two letters submitted online by the recommenders, unofficial transcripts accepted.

calendar.action: This is three days before the earliest applicant deadline and seven before the latest. Name three writers, list four or five for buffer. Fewer than two received means your application is not reviewed, whatever NSF's own pages say about whether you can still submit — the two pages disagree and this is the consequence both agree on. Chase your writers on 9 Oct and again on 14 Oct.
